question.text: An NPO client claims it qualifies as a Social Enterprise because '85% of its income has been applied for charitable purposes over the last 3 years'. Evaluating this for SSE eligibility, the SIA should note that:

answer.text: 85% income-application is the SEBI-ICDR primacy test and the NPO qualifies without further checks

85% is the Section 11 Income Tax threshold for tax exemption; it is NOT the SEBI-ICDR primacy test. An NPO must establish primacy of social intent via alignment with the 16 eligible activities and target underserved populations
85% is the CSR threshold under Section 135 — the NPO cannot claim SSE eligibility via this route
85% refers to the FCRA utilisation ratio and is unrelated to SSE

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The 85% threshold is under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act 1961 for income-application by charitable trusts. It is separate from SEBI-ICDR eligibility. An NPO must independently establish (a) engagement in at least one of the 16 eligible activities and (b) target underserved populations. The 67% threshold applies only to FPEs; NPOs demonstrate primacy through social intent and target-segment evidence, not a percentage test. **The Trap:** Option A conflates tax and SSE regimes. Option C misattributes to CSR. Option D is a fabricated FCRA ratio. Only B correctly distinguishes the two regimes. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to Ch 10 (Taxation — 85% Section 11), V-A (MF Distributor 80G), and X-A (Investment Adviser). SIAs must not validate SEBI-ICDR primacy via IT-Act tests. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** In your scoping memo, separate three tests: (a) legal form (Trust/Society/Section 8), (b) IT exemption (12AB, 85% application, 80G), (c) SEBI-ICDR primacy (16 activities + target + 67% if FPE). Issuing these as a checklist avoids cross-regime confusion during fieldwork.
